svg.aria-label: Two charts on the real model, on the conference task, with 10 seeds per point. Mean stall time with five coordinators killed: FractalSwarm 11.2 s, Ideal durable supervisor 21.9 s, Realistic durable supervisor 21.9 s, In-process supervisor 42.8 s. Mean extra cost against the same workflow with none killed: FractalSwarm +2.4%, Ideal durable supervisor +8.1%, Realistic durable supervisor +4.3%, In-process supervisor +67.0%. Why a tie, when the means differ: a win needs every seed to agree by a minimum effect, a rule fixed before the runs, and these seeds disagree. The in-process supervisor's workers run inside its process, so each crash cancels their calls. Most of the gap between it and the swarm comes from that design, so it is no evidence against a well-built supervisor. Extra cost is on the pre-registered basis, which estimates the cost of cancelled calls. On completed calls only, the swarm's is −1.1% against +29.2% for the in-process supervisor. The swarm stalled more with no crash than with five: no crash removes a stall, so this is what noise looks like.
